gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured figure for any deck sold new today: HomeTheaterHifi's John E. Johnson Jr. measured 0.52% RMS wow and flutter on the TEAC W-1200, recording and playing back his own test tones. That is twice TEAC's 0.25% spec. On the same tones the 1 kHz distortion was 1.9–2.6%, and the response on Type I tape was down 10 dB by 10 kHz.
standout_why: I read three rival pages. StereoNET's 2026 guide (cited in all three chats) gives no wow and flutter or speed figures for any deck. Its only numbers are maker claims for portables, such as FiiO CP13 SNR above 55 dB and We Are Rewind 30 Hz–14.5 kHz. It says new players are 'a healthy step behind' a serviced 1980s flagship but gives no measurement. Tape Lab (cited) has no measured figures at all. Portcycling (cited once) returned 403, so I couldn't check it. Hi-Fi Choice 055 (cited) was too large to open. It is a 1980s issue, so it cannot contain the W-1200 or 202MKVII, but it may hold period figures for the CR-7 or Dragon. None of the rivals puts a measured number on the 'new deck vs restored vintage' gap that ChatGPT's answer depends on.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's line that the W-1200 is 'not as high-fidelity as a restored vintage flagship' with a named measurement. The pick itself does not change. The W-1200 stays the best deck you can buy new, and the Tascam 202MKVII uses the same transport and lists the same 0.25% spec, so the measurement does not separate the two. The page should present the W-1200 as a deck for dubbing and digitizing, not for critical recording. Shoppers who mainly want recording quality should be pointed to a serviced three-head vintage deck.

findings.label: Wow and flutter, measured
findings.source_title: TEAC W-1200 Cassette Tape Deck Recorder/Player Review and Comparison with a Reel-to-Reel Tape Deck - HomeTheaterHifi.com
findings.note: John E. Johnson Jr., published 2025-02-03. This is a record-plus-playback figure from the reviewer's own recording, not a lab-grade flutter test tape. The reviewer blames part of the gap to spec on the missing calibration tape. Lynx sound card used as source and analyzer interface.

findings.label: 1 kHz THD+N off tape at 0 VU
findings.value: 1.88% (ATR Type I), 2.55% (ATR Type II), 2.05% (RTM Type I)
findings.source_title: TEAC W-1200 Cassette Tape Deck Recorder/Player Review and Comparison with a Reel-to-Reel Tape Deck - HomeTheaterHifi.com
findings.note: John E. Johnson Jr., 2025-02-03. New C-60 tapes recorded at 0 dB VU from a 1 V input; the deck has no bias adjustment. The record-monitor path with no tape measured 0.0078% THD+N, so the distortion comes from the tape stage.

findings.label: IMD (60 Hz / 7 kHz) off tape
findings.value: 54% (ATR Type I), 60% (ATR Type II), 32% (RTM Type I)
findings.source_title: TEAC W-1200 Cassette Tape Deck Recorder/Player Review and Comparison with a Reel-to-Reel Tape Deck - HomeTheaterHifi.com
findings.note: John E. Johnson Jr., 2025-02-03. Same setup as above. RTM Type I gave the best result of the three tapes.

findings.label: Treble response off tape
findings.value: Down 10 dB by 10 kHz on ATR Type I; about 2 dB better at 10 kHz on ATR Type II
findings.source_title: TEAC W-1200 Cassette Tape Deck Recorder/Player Review and Comparison with a Reel-to-Reel Tape Deck - HomeTheaterHifi.com
findings.note: John E. Johnson Jr., 2025-02-03. Recorded at 0 dB VU, which is a high level that compresses treble on cassette. TEAC's spec is 30 Hz–13 kHz ±4 dB (Type I) and 30 Hz–15 kHz ±4 dB (Type II), at unstated level.

findings.label: Same reviewer's reel-to-reel reference (Otari MX-5050-III-2, 15 ips)
findings.value: 0.09% wow and flutter; 1.17% IMD; response to about 23 kHz
findings.source_title: TEAC W-1200 Cassette Tape Deck Recorder/Player Review and Comparison with a Reel-to-Reel Tape Deck - HomeTheaterHifi.com
findings.note: John E. Johnson Jr., 2025-02-03. RTM SM900 tape at 0 VU, 1 V input. On the same rig, the reel deck measured about one-sixth the W-1200's wow and flutter (0.09% vs 0.52%).

findings.label: Dynamic range, measured
findings.value: About 54 dB (Type I), 56.5 dB (Type II), 59 dB (Type IV)
findings.note: Craig Stark, Stereo Review, March 1988, p. 56, as cited on Wikipedia. I could not open the original scan; the Stereo Review April 1983 PDF exceeded the fetch limit.

findings.label: Treble response on test tapes
findings.note: Craig Stark, Stereo Review, April 1983, p. 39, as cited on Wikipedia. Stark said this reflects the equipment that recorded the test tape, not the Dragon.

findings.label: Record/play upper frequency limit at −20 dB
findings.note: Roberson, Audio, May 1983, p. 70, as cited on Wikipedia. It is measured at −20 dB, so it is not comparable with the W-1200's 0 VU result above.

findings.label: Absolute speed error
findings.note: Keywood, Hi-Fi Review Buying Guide, 1987, p. 72, as cited on Wikipedia.

unsourced: Nakamichi Dragon measured wow and flutter (Stereo Review April 1983, Craig Stark: 0.016% wrms on a test tape, 0.017% wrms record/play forward). This appeared only in search snippets. Sound & Vision's 2018 reprint returned 403, the Stereo Review 1983-04 PDF on worldradiohistory exceeded the fetch size limit, and the High Fidelity 1983-04 scan and the per-page OCR PDF would not render as text.

Nakamichi CR-7A measured figures from Audio's August 1986 Equipment Profile. The gammaelectronics.xyz transcription failed on an SSL certificate error, I did not have approval to fetch it with curl, and the worldradiohistory Audio 1986-08 URL I tried returned 404.
Revox B215 measured figures from Audio's July 1985 Equipment Profile. The gammaelectronics.xyz page failed on the same SSL error.
Sony TC-KA7ES measured figures. I found only Sony's spec (0.022% WRMS) on audio-database.com and hifi-wiki in search results, and no magazine or lab test.

Tascam 202MKVII measured figures. Bonedo's German test showed no measurement section in search results, and I found no other bench test. Only Tascam's spec sheet figures exist (0.25% WRMS; 59 dB S/N).
TEAC AD-850-SE measured figures. I searched for none, and none appeared in any result.

A second W-1200 measurement by VWestlife (YouTube, reportedly 0.09–0.11% W RMS using TEAC's own flutter test tape). The Filmot transcript page returned 403 and I did not have approval to fetch the video page, so I could not open it.
